title: The Echo of the Kuiper Line
premise: Vesper Pemberton, a clone of a murdered woman, keeps the lonely Kuiper Line beacon as penance for a life she never chose. When gravity stutters system-wide for nine seconds, she finds a hidden signal in the beacon's logs: proof that the original Vesper discovered a fleet-ordered massacre on Meridian Station, erased from every archive. As the fragile truce between the Fleet and the Outer Colonies nears expiry, Vesper must gather a ragtag found family—a defector archivist, a smuggler, and the dead woman's estranged daughter—to authenticate records the Fleet will kill to bury. In the end, broadcasting the truth costs Vesper her anonymity and nearly her life, but it wins the colonies their seat at the table and gives her, at last, a name that belongs to herself.
about_author: Astrid Almeida is a former radio astronomer who traded telescope shifts for writing full-time after a decade listening to signals nobody else believed mattered. She lives aboard a converted survey vessel in the North Atlantic, where she writes stories about people who keep watch at the edges of things.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Alone at the beacon, she feels gravity flicker and watches every instrument flatline for nine seconds. The eerie calm afterward unsettles her more than the event itself. Emotional beat: isolation sharpened into dread—the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: The Woman I Was Before
chapters.summary: Flashback-laced chapter establishing Vesper's clone status, her legal non-personhood, and why she inherited the original's unsolved murder case along with the beacon posting. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grief for a self she never met, resentment braided with duty.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Reviewing the flicker's data, Vesper finds an encrypted burst embedded in the beacon's oldest log layer—timestamped the night the original died. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding fear; the case she inherited suddenly becomes hers to solve.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Defected
chapters.summary: Vesper travels to Ceres under a false manifest and meets Juno Reyes, a disgraced Fleet archivist who recognizes the encryption. POV alternates Vesper/Juno. Emotional beat: wary first contact—two people who trust no one testing whether they can trust each other.

chapters.title: Meridian Station Never Existed
chapters.summary: Juno reveals the decrypted fragment references Meridian Station, scrubbed from all charts. Eleven thousand colonists, unrecorded. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: guilt; Juno helped erase the station before she understood what she was erasing.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: To reach Meridian's coordinates, they hire Odile Brannigan, a smuggler whose brother was stationed there. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: anger and bargaining—Odile agrees only because Vesper promises her brother's name back into history.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Back-channel news: the Fleet-Colony truce expires in forty days, and hardliners on both sides want war. The massacre record could tip either way. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: pressure mounting; the personal quest becomes a political fuse.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Dead
chapters.summary: On Titan, they find Mara Pemberton, the original's daughter, who despises clones and refuses to help—until Vesper shows her her mother's final message. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief curdling into reluctant alliance; found family begins forming from broken pieces.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Deciphering more of the log, Vesper learns the beacon itself was built to broadcast the massacre evidence—and someone ordered it silenced, then assigned her to maintain it as a living lock. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: horror and betrayal; her exile was designed.

chapters.title: Fleet Shadow
chapters.summary: A Fleet audit vessel arrives at the beacon hunting the gravity anomaly's source. Vesper barely evades capture, losing her ship. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: paranoia; invisibility is officially over.

chapters.title: The Colony That Refused to Die
chapters.summary: At Meridian's drifting hulk, they find survivors' descendants living feral aboard the wreck, keeping oral histories of the massacre. POV: Odile reunites with her brother's old crewmate. Emotional beat: awe and sorrow; memory outlived the archives.

chapters.title: Testimony in Bone
chapters.summary: Physical evidence—mass graves, scorched bulkheads, a child's recorder—corroborates the digital fragment. But Fleet law requires authenticated chain-of-custody, which only Juno can forge. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: moral crisis; redemption means becoming a criminal again.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Fleet agents ambush them; Mara is captured and offered her mother's restored estate in exchange for denouncing the evidence. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: temptation versus loyalty; she chooses the strangers who became family over the lie that would restore her name.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Day
chapters.summary: A recovered diary reconstructs the original Vesper's final hours: she hid the key inside the beacon and named her clone heir deliberately, trusting even a stranger-copy over the Fleet. POV: interwoven past/present. Emotional beat: reconciliation; Vesper stops resenting the woman she was cloned from.

chapters.title: Gravity Remembers
chapters.summary: They discover the nine-second flicker was Meridian's mass being briefly re-registered by the system's gravitational network—the universe itself testifying. Juno realizes the beacon can trigger a permanent re-registration. POV: Juno/Vesper. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline; the truce expires in six days.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Airlock
chapters.summary: One of the Meridian descendants is a Fleet informant. He sabotages the beacon's transmitter array and escapes with half the authentication keys. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: devastation; the found family fractures under suspicion.

chapters.title: Repairing Trust
chapters.summary: Stranded and hunted, the group must rebuild the array together. Old wounds surface—Odile's brother, Juno's complicity, Mara's prejudice—but shared labor mends what words couldn't. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: quiet reconciliation; belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Forty Hours
chapters.summary: With the truce hours from expiring, the Fleet blockade closes in. Vesper must physically climb the beacon's external spine to hand-splice the final conduit during a micrometeorite storm. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; the invisible woman makes herself unmistakable.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. The beacon fires the re-registration pulse: Meridian Station blazes back onto every chart in the system, its eleven thousand names restored, the massacre undeniable. The Fleet blockade hesitates as colonies mobilize—not for war, but witness. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: triumph laced with cost; Vesper takes a round meant for the transmitter.

chapters.title: The Hearing of Record
chapters.summary: Wounded but alive, Vesper testifies via relay as the truce is renegotiated around the revealed truth. Hardliners fall; the colonies gain representation. Juno surrenders to face charges, her forged chain-of-custody accepted as necessary. POV: Mara watching. Emotional beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Resolution begins. Legally recognized as a person, Vesper declines the original's estate and instead petitions to keep the beacon—recommissioned openly this time—as a memorial. The found family scatters to new purposes but stays tethered. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: peace; duty transformed from sentence into vocation.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: Final chapter. One year later, Vesper maintains the beacon with visitors now—Mara's letters, Odile's smuggling runs, Juno's parole visits. When a young runaway clone arrives seeking shelter, Vesper opens the airlock without hesitation. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: belonging complete; the echo of one woman's murder has become a home for many.
